metadataReview.note: The attack began on 21 September 1809, as dated in the contemporary Royal Collection print and the Ministry of Culture account of the first battery assaulted. This review aligns the original 20 September start to the documented combat; it does not date the expedition’s preparations. The retained end, 28 September, denotes British withdrawal after occupation and destruction of defences, not eight days of uninterrupted fighting. The retained Wikidata event coordinate is a coarse Saint-Paul Bay anchor with one arcminute source precision, not the measured position of a ship, battery or the landing farther north.

inclusionReview.note: Reviewed inclusion of the individual amphibious attack on Saint-Paul, Réunion, in September 1809. The Royal Collection contemporary print names the British squadron, its action against the French frigate Caroline and the assault on a shore battery on 21 September. Ministry of Culture archaeology independently identifies the attack on the Embouchure battery that morning. This is a concrete combined naval and land engagement, distinct from the wider Mauritius campaign and the invasion of the island in 1810; the broad source class naval warfare is not made generally eligible. The raid continued through the British withdrawal on 28 September.

qualifiers.cohort: Six named vessels in Rowley’s British squadron, including the East India Company schooner Wasp.

strength.note: Six ships are explicitly enumerated in the contemporary print inscription and independently counted by the ONF panel. This is the naval squadron, including its supporting vessels, not a count of the separate landing force or of ships all firing simultaneously. Captured merchant ships are not added to either naval strength.

name.fr: Force de débarquement britannique de Keating

qualifiers.cohort: Keating’s mixed military landing force at the Rivière-des-Galets mouth, advancing on Saint-Paul on 21 September 1809
qualifiers.interpretation: Rounded personnel estimate from the ONF interpretation panel; soldiers denotes military personnel, including the landed seamen and marines, not exclusively Army infantry.

strength.note: Approximately 600 military personnel in the British landing force, using the ONF panel’s rounded figure for the 21 September landing and advance. This includes the mixed soldiers, marines and seamen employed ashore; it is not a count of all crews aboard the six ships, and it is not added to ship strength. No later garrison or reinforcement total is inferred.

note:
Amphibious raid: naval and land components retain distinct units and two sourced opposing camps. The British squadron contains six named vessels. The complete French naval and land strengths remain unquantified; the named frigate Caroline is not treated as the entire French side, and recaptured British Indiamen are not converted into French combatants. The ONF panel’s rounded 600 is retained as an approximate strength of Keating’s military landing force on 21 September, including soldiers, marines and seamen employed ashore; it is not a total of all ship crews or a later garrison strength. Ship and personnel units remain separate. No ship or human loss totals are assigned, and empty losses mean unknown rather than zero. No equipment profile is assigned by this review. The main assault occurred on 21 September; the retained 28 September end denotes withdrawal. The original coarse bay coordinate is not an exact ship position.
